subject: OptiMed SLOs & deployment follow-up
summary: Post-call recap confirming OptiMed pain points (latency and cost at peak), goals (p95/p99 targets), and proposed Redwood deployment topology (dedicated pool + KV caching, regional failover). Next steps: share prompt set & schedule technical deep-dive with OptiMed infra lead.
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Laurent Dubois <laurent@optimed.ai>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@optimed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: OptiMed production goals & SLOs (next steps)

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation and a clear set of priorities. Quick recap so we're aligned and can plan the technical deep-dive: 

1) Top pain points you shared
- P95 latency spikes during morning batch jobs and campaign bursts are impacting clinical UX.
- Cost is a concern for sustained inference at scale; you want predictable unit economics.
- Auditability and per-request tracing for SOC/audit purposes (low-latency logs) are required for procurement.

2) Goals we heard
- Target p95 <= 250ms for standard clinical prompts; p99 to be under ~750ms as a stretch target.
- Support steady-state ~150 req/s with peaks up to ~250 req/s.
- Prefer a private or dedicated deployment (VPC) for data controls; must support KMS integration.

3) Model / workload notes from the call
- Primary workload: clinical summarization + triage prompts; median prompt ~120 tokens, typical generated length ~80 tokens, 10% of requests can be longer (up to 800 tokens).
- You expect a 1:1 read/write ratio for inference calls vs background processing.

4) Initial topology ideas (high level)
- Recommend Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved baseline capacity) in us-west with failover to us-east.
- Use quantized open-models (13B/70B variants) depending on quality tests; prefer starting with Llama2-13B-8bit for baseline cost/latency.
- Enable continuous KV/prefix caching for multi-turn sessions and configure batching with per-route targets to keep latency SLOs.

5) Asks / next steps
- Please share a small sample prompt set + token-length distribution (we can use redacted data).
- Confirm compliance checklist items (SOC2 scope + any specific retention needs).
- Tech deep-dive proposed: 60–90m with your infra lead (Raj) and our runtime engineers — available propose Aug 11, 10:00am PT.

Attachments: optimed_prod_requirements.xlsx (placeholder that we discussed), draft architecture image referenced during call.

I'll follow up internally to sketch a Dedicated-sizing proposal and bring Neha from our inference infra team into that thread.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laurent Dubois <laurent@optimed.ai>

Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@optimed.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@optimed.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: OptiMed production goals & SLOs (next steps)

Thanks, Avery — that's a helpful summary. Confirming a few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic profile: our product analytics team expects steady-state ~150 req/s, with marketing-driven spikes up to ~250 req/s for short periods (10–15 minutes).
- Token distribution: median ~110 tokens, 95th percentile ~420 tokens. We've attached a small sample latency file (optimed_latency_sample.csv) from a staging run that shows current p95 around 600ms on our self-hosted model.
- Compliance: SOC2 in scope; we also need per-request audit IDs in logs and the ability to redact PHI before logs leave our VPC.

We like the Dedicated approach you suggest. Raj — looping you in to coordinate the deep technical session and to share any infra constraints (on-prem connectors, VPN, firewall egress rules).

Happy to book Aug 11 at 10:00am PT if that works for Redwood.

— Laurent

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Laurent Dubois <laurent@optimed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: OptiMed production goals & SLOs (next steps)

Thanks — jumping in with a rough technical sizing and options so we have something concrete to discuss on the deep-dive. Notes below are preliminary and will be refined once we get your prompt set / token distribution: 

Option A (cost-conscious, low-latency):
- Model: Llama2-13B quantized to 8-bit FP; estimated p95 ~120–220ms at 150 rps with an appropriately sized pool.
- Hardware: Dedicated pool of 6 x A10G or 4 x A100-40GB (reserve baseline), autoscale +2 nodes for bursts.
- Batching: target dynamic batch size up to ~32 tokens; prefer short-response batching to keep p95 low.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching with 30-minute TTL for session reuse; store hot prefixes in local NVMe cache on nodes to avoid remote fetches.

Option B (quality-first, higher COA):
- Model: Llama2-70B mixed-precision/4-bit quant; expected better generation quality but ~2–3x cost. Aim for p95 ~220–400ms depending on sequence length.
- Hardware: 2–3 x 80GB GPUs per model shard (we can propose sharding layout in the deep-dive).

Operational recommendations:
- Reserve Dedicated baseline to hit predictable throughput and attach burst capacity for marketing spikes.
- Autoscale policy: target 65–75% GPU utilization to maintain headroom for p95 SLOs.
- Tracing: enable token-level sampling at 1% and request-level logging with a redaction hook for PHI before logs leave your VPC (Redwood supports on-prem redaction hooks).
- Fallbacks: configure multi-variant routing (13B as fallback to 70B) to keep the service available if large models are constrained.

Questions for your infra team before the deep-dive:
- Can you share expected egress rules / IP whitelist constraints and whether you require an on-prem air-gap connector?
- Do you have KMS provider preference (AWS KMS vs Azure KeyVault)?

I'll prepare a compact Dedicated-sizing PDF for our call (attaching redwood_dedicated_proposal.pdf). If you can share the prompt file and a short sample of 100 requests, we can run a quick micro-benchmark to validate these numbers before the call.

— Neha

- Raj will prepare a short doc with our current firewall/egress constraints and preferred KMS (Raj copied).
- Meeting confirmed: Aug 11, 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive. Raj, Sarah (CS lead), and I will attend; please send a calendar invite.

Marissa / Avery — if you can include the sizing PDF and an agenda for the 60–90 minute session that would be great. We're also fine with Redwood bringing a small runtime team to discuss KV cache and autoscaling specifics.

Look forward to the deep-dive.

— Laurent
